stimulus.content:
In many conversations, a pause of even a few seconds can make people uncomfortable. Someone quickly says something, anything, to fill the gap. (1) [[u:It is as if silence were an empty space that must be filled before it becomes embarrassing.]]

However, silence is not always empty. In some cultures, a short pause before answering shows that the listener is taking the question seriously. (2) [[u:To reply too quickly may even suggest that one has not thought about what the other person said.]] When people from such different backgrounds talk to each other, a pause that one person intends as respect can be taken by the other as a lack of interest.

(3) [[u:Misunderstandings of this kind are hard to notice, because neither speaker is aware that the other is following different rules.]] Each simply concludes that the other person is rude or unfriendly.

The solution is not to decide which rule is correct. It is to recognize that the meaning of silence, like the meaning of words, depends on the people who share it. (4) [[u:The more we are aware of this, the less likely we are to judge others by standards they never agreed to.]]
